name: Macedonian
confidence_why: 5 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 3 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_quote: A word followed by enclitics automatically forms with them a group subject to the antepenult rule: the stress falls on the antepenult of the whole group as a unit.
sweep_summary: Four titles, all judged; none contradicts the catalog. Two were downloaded open and read: Harizanov 2014 (FASL 22, author preprint) §4.1.1 and Bennett, Harizanov & Henderson 2018 (LI 49, accepted-manuscript preprint from Bennett's UCSC site, also lingbuzz 003413) §2.2 both state regular antepenultimate stress with initial stress in 1-2 syllable words and locate the domain in the minimal prosodic word, which includes post-verbal enclitics but excludes ordinary preverbal clitics (enlarged domains under negation/wh; Monosyllabic Head Effect gives penult with monosyllabic verbs). These confirm and refine the catalog's fixed-strict antepenult coding and its word(+enclitic-group) domain quote from Lunt 1952 §1.421; Lunt remains the deciding reference-grammar source and is not superseded. Hagberg 1993/2006 (already held by the project from the capa1241 search, IA scan; Glottolog's MPG handle is bot-blocked) uses Macedonian as a secondary theoretical case on p. 49-50: regular antepenult plus loanword penult/final exceptions that revert to antepenult under suffixation — confirms. Franks 1987 (IJSLP 35-36: 93-142), already in our bibliography, could not be obtained: no DOI, archive. it stays print only at high acquisition priority as the fullest dedicated treatment of the exception classes and phrasal stress domains. Side note from the held store record (source_audit_2026-09-16/): it already flags that the catalog's domain quote sits on Lunt printed p. 22, not p. 21. all lookups were by direct download.

(8) a. proizVEduva 'produce (3sg.impfv.prs)' b. proIZvede 'produce (3sg.pst)' c. PROizvod 'product' d. VOdi 'lead (3sg.impfv.prs)' e. new_statements.reading: Fixed antepenultimate word stress (initial in words of one or two syllables), computed over the minimal prosodic word, which takes in post-predicate enclitics but not ordinary preverbal clitics; negation and wh-words create an enlarged stress domain. This is exactly the catalog's fixed-strict antepenult coding with domain word extended to the enclitic group (Lunt 1952 §1.421), now stated in a 2018 peer-reviewed source with an explicit prosodic-word domain analysis.

new_statements.quote: The Western Macedonian dialect area that includes the central Macedonian dialects has threesyllabic accentual system, i.e. the stress in threesyllabic and polysyllabic words and in some syntagmatic units falls on the third syllable from the end of the word: vodˈeniʦa, vodenˈiʦata, ne-mu-sˈe-sluʃa, etc. As it is evident from the examples and when the number of syllables is increased due to adding the definite article or the plural ending, the stress moves in order occur on the third syllable from the end of the word.
new_statements.citation: Friedman, Victor A. 1993. Macedonian. In B. Comrie & G. Corbett (eds.), The Slavonic Languages, 249-305. London: Routledge.
new_statements.locator: Labroska, Markovikj & Friedman 2026, section on Vidoeski's classification, p. 182 (p. 18); see also §2.2.2 (Kepeski 1946 classification) pp. 173-174 and p. 183
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (extracted text of the saved PDF, 24 form feeds = 25 pages, printed 165-188): the quoted passage is at lines 755-761, i.e. after 17 form feeds = p. 18 = printed p. 182 (the '182' footer follows it), word for word including the source's own 'in order occur on the third syllable' and 'threesyllabic accentual system'. Surrounding text (p. 182) continues: 'The trisyllabic accent in the western dialect area also has a syntagmatic character, i.e. syntagmatic units, usually clitics plus an accentual word, can be used as a stress unit with one accent, for example: pˈod-voda, zˈ-raka, ˈod-srʦe, sˈo-tebe, ʧitˈajci-go, donesˈi-mi-go' — exactly the clitic-group refinement the compiler reports. The…
new_statements.relation_note: The statement is from Labroska, Markovikj & Friedman 2026, not from Friedman 1993 (which has no open copy: Friedman's UChicago CV lists the chapter without a PDF link; the 2003 revised version in Dve makedonski gramatiki is also unlinked). It agrees with the catalog's fixed antepenult coding (antepenultimate stress) and with the Bennett et al. 2018 statement for the standard/Western variety, and adds the clitic-group domain and a dialect map (SW penult, East free/mobile, border dialects paradigmatically fixed). Bonus corroboration by the same author, also downloaded and saved ( = Friedman 2002, Macedonian, LW/M 117, Lincom; open SEELRC copy), §1.3 Prosody p. 12: 'Literary Macedonian has fix…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the Western (central) dialects, which the article says are the basis of the standard language (p. 173: 'Central (Veles, Prilep, Kichevo, Bitola) – with fixed accent on the third syllable from the end of the word. This dialect is the basis of Macedonian standard language.'), stress falls on the third syllable from the end and moves rightward when the article or plural ending adds syllables; clitic-plus-word groups form one accentual unit with the same antepenultimate placement (p. 182: pˈod-voda, ʧitˈajci-go, donesˈi-mi-go).
new_statements.exceptions: Dialect variation only (no lexical exceptions discussed): Southwestern (Kostur-Lerin) dialects have penultimate stress (p. 174); Kukush-Voden 'mobile accent with a tendency towards penultima' (p. 174); the easternmost Southeastern dialects 'have free and mobile stress that can be placed on any syllable in the word: glˈava, glavˈata, nidˈelta, iskarˈal, grabnˈale' (p. 183); dialects on the west-east border have stress that is 'free but paradigmatically fixed: jadˈex, jadˈeʃe, jadˈexme' (p. 183); northern dialects are 'not consistent' (p. 183). In the Southeastern area unstressed vowels are reduced or elided (p. 183).
new_statements.identity_note: The catalog record is standard Macedonian, whose norm is based on the West-Central dialects (Veles-Prilep-Bitola-Kichevo); both opened works say so explicitly. Labroska, Markovikj & Friedman 2026 describes the whole dialect continuum (Western antepenult; Southwestern penult; Southeastern/Eastern mobile or free; northern mixed), and Friedman 2002 §0.5.3 gives the same dialect survey (Western antepenult in the Republic, penult in Greece and Albania; Eastern non-fixed).

sources.note: Fixed antepenultimate stress (initial in 1-2 syllable words) in the Western dialects on which the standard is based; domain is the minimal prosodic word, which includes post-predicate clitics (doNEsi go, doneSI mi go, Rudin et al. 1999:551) but excludes ordinary preverbal clitics (mi go DAle, *mi GO dale). Under negation and wh-words an 'enlarged stress domain' forms (ne GO vide, kako SE vikaš); the Monosyllabic Head Effect (Franks 1989) gives penultimate stress when the verb is monosyllabic (ne mu GO dal). Independently corroborates the catalog antepenultimate stress and the word(+enclitics)…

sources.citation: Harizanov, Boris. 2014. The role of prosody in the linearization of clitics: Evidence from Bulgarian and Macedonian. Formal Approaches to Slavic Linguistics 22: The McMaster Meeting 2013, 109-130. Ann Arbor: Michigan Slavic Publications.
sources.quote: Macedonian has regular antepenultimate stress and initial stress in mono- or disyllabic words. Relevant for the present purposes is that postverbal clitics affect stress placement, shifting it to the antepenultimate syllable (as has been reported to be the case in Indonesian, Latin, and Modern Greek): (19)a. doneSI 'bring' b. doNEsi go 'bring it' c. doneSI mi go 'bring it to me' [...] To capture these patterns, I assume that the domain of stress assignment in Macedonian is the minimal Prosodic Word, while the domain of morphophonemic alternations like vowel deletion of the kind described above is the maximal Prosodic Word.
sources.locator: §4.1.1 'Macedonian', author preprint p. 10 of 20 (preprint carries no journal page numbers; published pp. 109-130)
sources.note: A clitic-linearization paper (sole author Harizanov despite Glottolog's four-author listing), but §4.1.1 states the rule outright: regular antepenultimate stress, initial in 1-2 syllable words; postverbal (enclitic) object clitics count in the three-syllable window (doNEsi go, doneSI mi go); preverbal clitics are outside the window except under sentential negation and wh-questions (ne GO vide, zošto mu GO dade). Domain = minimal Prosodic Word.

sources.quote: Macedonian has regular antepenultimate stress as well as a few words which are exceptionally stressed on either the penult or final syllable (Lunt 1952, Comrie 1976, Franks 1983, Halle and Vergnaud 1987b, Hammond 1989b). Examples are given below. (4) Macedonian Stress: (a) Regular Antepenultimate Stress: vodéničar miller, vodénica mill, pólkovnik colonel, rábota work, véčer evening, zbór word (b) Exceptional Penult and Final Stress: konzumátor consumer, literatúra literature, komunízam communism, autobús bus, citát quotation, restorán restaurant
sources.locator: Ch. 2, printed p. 49 (IA p. 53), continuing to p. 50 with examples (4)-(5)
sources.note: Secondary (theoretical) use of Macedonian, data from Lunt/Comrie/Franks/Halle-Vergnaud/Hammond: regular antepenultimate stress with a closed set of loanword exceptions on penult/final; on suffixation the exceptions revert to antepenult (konzumátor-i, autobús-ite), argued to require lexical accents rather than lexical feet. scanned of the IA text garbles diacritics ('penulit', 'autobts'); readings above normalized from the displayed examples. Confirms the catalog class; adds nothing on domain.
